label: Clayton and Taylor: before modernity the theistic proofs were not intended as stand-alone proofs…
paraphrase: Clayton and Taylor (as reported): before modernity the theistic proofs were not intended as stand-alone proofs to convince an unbeliever; they operated within a theological theater, used within religious communities to correct heresy, confirm belief or express wonder, and apologetically mostly towards other theists such as Muslims; only later did 'the world' and 'reason' take the secular, disembedded sense of a neutral starting point.
